en: The Triplet of the Visible (Sanidassanattika), The Triplet of the Clung-to (Upādinnattika)

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, acquired, and subject to clinging, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive, and is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] in the case of root; six in the case of conascence … pe … six in the case of non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is visible and reactive, and not acquired but subject to clinging, [there arises] a state that is not visible and reactive, and not not-acquired but subject to clinging … [and so forth].
A state is related to a state by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. Nine [ways] with respect to the object; three with respect to the immediate; ... pe ...
nine with respect to decisive support and prenascence; ... pe ... nine with respect to non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reacting, not grasped, and not subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not non-demonstrable and non-reacting... [and so forth].

A state that is neither clung-to nor subject to clinging arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. There are six under the root condition, six under the predominance condition … pe … six under the non-disappearance condition.
